This passage describes a shell-and-tube heat exchanger that is installed in a refinery preheat train, where its role is to heat crude oil before the oil passes to the downstream processing units. The exchanger delivers a duty of 469 kW. On the hot side, the heating stream enters the exchanger at a temperature of 150 °C and leaves it at a temperature of 110 °C. On the cold side, the crude oil enters at 30 °C and is heated to an outlet temperature of 50 °C.

It may also be noted that the hot stream cools by 40 K across the exchanger, while the crude oil stream warms by 20 K. The temperature differences at the two ends of the exchanger can be worked out from these figures. At the hot end the difference is 100 K, obtained from 150 - 50, and at the cold end it is 80 K, obtained from 110 - 30. Combining these two differences gives a log-mean temperature difference of 89.6 K for the exchanger. The installed heat-transfer area is 39.9 m2, and the overall heat-transfer coefficient that corresponds to the stated duty is 131 W m-2 K-1.

With regard to fouling, it should be noted that the assessment of fouling is based on a single run lasting 90 days. No cleaning cycle has yet been completed for this exchanger, which means that the behaviour of the coefficient of 131 W m-2 K-1 over longer periods of operation remains uncertain.
target:
A shell-and-tube exchanger in a refinery crude-oil preheat train delivers a duty of 469 kW. The hot stream enters at 150 °C and leaves at 110 °C; the crude oil enters at 30 °C and leaves at 50 °C.

Terminal temperature differences are 100 K at the end where the hot stream enters (150 - 50) and 80 K at the other end (110 - 30), and the log-mean temperature difference taken from them is 89.6 K. The hot stream cools by 40 K across the exchanger and the crude oil warms by 20 K. Installed area is 39.9 m2. The overall coefficient that carries the stated duty over that area at that temperature difference is 131 W m-2 K-1.

The duty is a joint property of the two streams: the heat that leaves the hot stream enters the oil, and the overall coefficient states how much installed area that transfer requires at the temperature difference the streams provide. A larger area would carry the same duty at a smaller temperature difference, and a smaller area would demand a larger one; area and temperature difference are the two sides of the same design balance.

Fouling in the exchanger was assessed from a single 90-day run, and no cleaning cycle has been completed. The coefficient of 131 W m-2 K-1 is therefore the value for the state reached within that run. How the coefficient changes over a full operating cycle, and what cleaning restores, are both unknown on the present evidence.
